uncited: RotateY is a geometric transformation primitive that rotates a point or shape around the Y-axis in 3D space.
It serves as a fundamental building block for constructing camera poses and deforming Signed Distance Fields (SDFs).

Unlike [Rotation Transformation](2279-rotation-transformation.md), which may imply a general rotation matrix, RotateY specifically isolates the Y-axis component, and unlike [Twist](1722-twist.md), it applies a uniform rotation angle to the entire object rather than a spatially varying one.
It is a sibling to [RotateX](2278-rotatex.md) and [RotateZ](2280-rotatez.md).
- Input: A 3D point $P = (x, y, z)$ and a rotation angle $\theta$ (in radians or degrees, depending on implementation convention).
The input point is typically represented as a 3-component vector.
The rotation occurs in the XZ plane, leaving the Y-coordinate invariant.
For large numbers of cumulative rotations, consider normalizing the angle to $[0, 2\pi)$ to avoid precision loss.
Requires two multiplications, two additions/subtractions, and two trigonometric evaluations per point.
Cannot represent combined rotations without composition.
RotateY is a standard elementary transformation in computer graphics, derived from the fundamental rotation matrices in linear algebra.
It is widely used in raymarching shaders for SDF deformation and in camera pose construction to orient the view direction.
